logs.title: Log collection
logs.intro: OPNexus regularly fetches firewall logs from all hosts and stores them in its own database (see “Logs”). Longer retention means more storage, depending on the traffic volume of the connected firewalls — on heavily used hosts, even a few days can take up several gigabytes.
logs.maxSizeHint: 0 = unlimited. When the limit is reached the oldest entries are deleted. The value is estimated from the table size; Postgres does not hand freed space back to the file system but reuses it for new logs.

update.title: Update OPNexus
update.hint: Pulls the new images, switches the services and checks that everything is healthy. If that fails, OPNexus rolls back to the previous version automatically.
update.feedOff: The version check is off. Switch it on above so OPNexus can detect new versions.
update.feedHint: Regularly asks the release feed whether a newer version has been published. Only a plain request (GET) carrying your own version number is sent, nothing else. Off by default.
update.feedManaged: The version check is fixed by UPDATE_CHECK_URL in the server's .env and cannot be changed here.
update.feedError: The release feed is currently unreachable.
update.notEnabledTitle: Updates from the web interface are not enabled.
update.notEnabledBody: They need a small separate service (the updater) with access to Docker — deliberately optional. To enable it:
update.notEnabledStep1: Add to the .env on the server:
update.notEnabledImages: This only works with release images (release bundle, or OPNEXUS_IMAGE_REPO in the .env). If you build OPNexus from source, update with “git pull” and “docker compose up -d --build”.
update.notEnabledCli: Until then, update on the server with “opnexus update”.
update.unreachable: The updater does not respond. Check on the server: docker compose ps updater
update.localMode: This installation does not use release images (OPNEXUS_IMAGE_REPO is not set in the .env). Update on the server with “git pull” and “docker compose up -d --build”.
update.majorChange: Version {latest} is a major version jump. Please read the release notes first, then update on the server with “opnexus update {latest}”.
update.confirmBody: OPNexus pulls the new images and restarts itself. The interface is unavailable for about one to two minutes; the managed firewalls are not affected.
update.confirmSafety: A backup is taken automatically before a database migration. If the new version does not become healthy, OPNexus rolls back to the previous version on its own.
update.reconnecting: Reconnecting — this is normal while the services restart.

result.succeededUpdate: OPNexus is now running {version}. Reloading the page …

rollback.dataLoss: The update migrated the database. Rolling back restores the state from before the update: changes made since the update and the log history are lost.
rollback.noDataLoss: The database was not migrated — no data is lost.

ipsec.title: IPsec VPN (site-to-site)
ipsec.intro: Site-to-site tunnels with a pre-shared key, maintained centrally and deployed to firewalls or device groups. Unlike firewall rules there is no automatic rollback: a failed service reload can cut the connection OPNexus uses to reach the firewall. One phase 2 per tunnel and simple network-to-network tunnels are supported (no certificates/EAP, no pools).

ovpn.title: OpenVPN instances
ovpn.intro: OpenVPN instances (server or client), maintained centrally and deployed to firewalls or device groups. As with IPsec there is no automatic rollback: a failed service reload can cut the connection OPNexus uses to reach the firewall. Every target firewall must already have a certificate and CA (selected from its certificate store); optional TLS protection (tls-auth/tls-crypt) via a static key is supported, but no “shared key” instances without a certificate.

wg.title: WireGuard tunnels
wg.intro: WireGuard connections (one server interface and exactly one peer per tunnel), maintained centrally and deployed to firewalls or device groups. As with IPsec there is no automatic rollback: a failed service reload can cut the connection OPNexus uses to reach the firewall. You generate and enter the keys yourself; a pre-shared key per peer is optional.

auditExport.title: Audit export
auditExport.intro: Forwards the audit trail (who changed what, with status) to a syslog server and/or a webhook, so it also exists outside OPNexus. Only new events are sent from the moment you switch it on; firewall object contents are never included. Delivery is at least once: every event carries its id.

backupSettings.title: Backups
backupSettings.intro: Takes a configuration backup of every firewall on a schedule and keeps the newest ones. Optionally a copy is encrypted here with your passphrase and uploaded to S3-compatible storage (AWS S3, MinIO, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, Cloudflare R2, Hetzner…), so a lost OPNexus server or a lost firewall is not the end of your configuration. Delete old offsite copies with the bucket's lifecycle rules.

overlay.title: Management tunnel
overlay.intro: Lets OPNexus manage firewalls that have no public address (behind NAT, CGNAT, a mobile link). Each firewall dials out to a WireGuard hub on this server; OPNexus then reaches its API through the tunnel. Nothing on the firewall has to be reachable from the internet. Needed on the server: the hub container (COMPOSE_PROFILES=overlay) and a UDP port reachable from the internet.

variables.intro: Rules, aliases and NAT entries can contain placeholders like {{LAN_NET}}. Each firewall fills them with its own value, so one object serves many sites with different networks. sso.title: Single sign-on (OIDC)
sso.intro: Lets people sign in with your identity provider (Authentik, Keycloak, Entra ID, Google, …) instead of a password stored here. Roles come from the provider's groups at every login; without a mapped group nobody gets in. Local accounts keep working, so you can always sign in with the admin password if the provider is down.

welcome.title: Welcome to OPNexus
welcome.intro: OPNexus manages your OPNsense firewalls in one place: rules, NAT, VPN, certificates, updates and HA clusters. This assistant sets up the essentials in a few minutes. You can skip it at any time and reopen it later under System › Setup.

points.account: Secure the account: your own password and two-factor sign-in.

rollouts.title: Rollouts
rollouts.intro: Firmware updates in waves: a small group first (canary), then pilot, then the rest. Between waves OPNexus waits a soak time and checks the health of the updated firewalls. On anything unusual the rollout stops and notifies you. Each host goes through the normal scheduled maintenance (backup, CARP handover, audit).

analysis.title: Rule analysis
analysis.intro: Answers which firewall rule decides the first packet of a connection (source, destination, protocol, port). Read-only; nothing is changed on any firewall.

form.title: Connection
form.srcHint: A single IPv4 or IPv6 address, not a host name or network.
form.protoHint: tcp, udp, icmp, another protocol name or a protocol number (0-255).
form.dportHint: Without a port, the verdict stays unknown for rules that restrict the port.
form.sportHint: Empty = any port from the ephemeral range.
form.icmptypeHint: Name or number, e.g. echoreq or 8.
form.ifaceHint: The interface the packet arrives on. Automatic guesses from the source IP and is marked as probable.
form.egressHint: Also checks the outbound rules on the interface towards the destination. Traffic only counts as allowed if both sides let it through.
form.refreshHint: Reads the rules fresh from the firewall instead of using data cached for up to 60 seconds.
form.missing: Source and destination IP are required.

empty.title: Which rule matches?
empty.description: Enter source and destination; the result appears here and the query lives in the address bar so you can share it.

noHosts.title: No firewalls
noHosts.description: At least one firewall must be connected for the analysis.

result.hostError: This host could not be evaluated.
result.decisiveIfKnown: Most likely rule if the open points do not apply
result.noRuleHint: No rule entry matches; the packet filter (pf) then lets the packet through.
result.unresolvedHint: The source IP belongs to no interface network. Choose the ingress interface manually.
result.undecidedHint: At least one unclear rule could change the result. This is not a verdict; resolve the open points below.
result.rulesLinkHint: Opens the live rules. Look for rule {id} on {host}.
result.noLink: Automatic or legacy rule: not editable in OPNexus
result.quickHint: quick: this rule decides immediately; no further rules are checked.

tip.sure: All rules could be checked unambiguously.
tip.probable: The verdict relies on assumptions or an unclear rule that would not change the outcome.
tip.unknown: An unclear rule could change the result. There is no reliable verdict.
tip.unresolved: Nothing can be checked without an ingress interface.

trace.title: Why?
trace.hint: All rules in the order the packet filter (pf) checks them. The last match wins unless a quick rule matches earlier.

notes.IFACE_GUESSED_hint: The ingress interface was derived from the source IP, not given. Choose it manually to be sure.
notes.EGRESS_GUESSED_hint: The egress interface was derived from the destination IP.
notes.IFACE_UNRESOLVED_hint: No interface could be determined for the source IP.
notes.EGRESS_UNRESOLVED_hint: No egress interface could be determined for the destination IP; the egress side was not checked.
notes.NAT_NEARBY_hint: A port forward matches this connection. Filter rules see the address after translation, so the verdict is only probable.
notes.NAT_UNAVAILABLE_hint: The firewall's port forwards could not be read; a translation cannot be ruled out.
notes.POLICY_ROUTE_hint: The deciding rule sends the traffic through a specific gateway.
notes.STATELESS_hint: The rule keeps no state. Reply packets need a rule of their own.
notes.SCHEDULE_NOW_hint: The rule has a schedule and is currently loaded according to the firewall.
notes.RULES_NOT_LOADED_hint: Enabled rules are not in the loaded ruleset (for example because of a schedule) and were skipped.
notes.PF_RULESET_UNAVAILABLE_hint: The loaded pf ruleset could not be read, so order and load state are only estimated.
notes.ORDER_MISMATCH_hint: The order in the configuration does not match the loaded ruleset.
notes.ORDER_GUESSED_hint: The order of some rules could not be proven and was estimated.
notes.TCP_FLAGS_hint: The rule checks TCP flags; the first packet (SYN) probably matches it, but not certainly.
notes.RATE_LIMIT_hint: The rule limits connections; above the limit it may behave differently.
notes.PF_DEFAULT_PASS_hint: No rule matches; the packet filter (pf) then lets the packet through.
notes.QUICK_UNKNOWN_hint: For one rule it is unclear whether it decides immediately.
notes.GROUPS_UNAVAILABLE_hint: Interface groups could not be read; rules for groups are unclear.
notes.ALIASES_UNAVAILABLE_hint: The alias list could not be read; rules using aliases are unclear.
notes.ALIAS_REFERENCES_UNAVAILABLE_hint: The firewall could not tell whether the addresses are in aliases.

unknown.ALIAS_MISSING_hint: A rule refers to an alias that does not exist on the firewall.
unknown.ALIAS_TABLE_UNAVAILABLE_hint: The alias's pf table could not be queried (for example Geo-IP or URL list).
unknown.ALIAS_CYCLE_hint: Aliases refer to each other in a loop.
unknown.ALIAS_TOO_DEEP_hint: The alias nesting is too deep to evaluate.
unknown.ALIAS_EXCLUSION_hint: An alias contains exclusions that cannot be evaluated reliably.
unknown.FQDN_UNRESOLVED_hint: A host name in an alias could not be resolved to addresses.
unknown.TAGGED_hint: A rule only applies to tagged packets. The tag is set by another rule that did not match here.
unknown.PORT_NOT_GIVEN_hint: Without a destination port it is unclear whether a rule restricted to ports matches.
unknown.SRC_PORT_NOT_GIVEN_hint: A rule restricts the source port, which was not given.
unknown.PORT_ALIAS_UNRESOLVED_hint: A port alias could not be resolved.
unknown.PORT_UNPARSEABLE_hint: A port specification in a rule could not be interpreted.
unknown.ICMP_TYPE_NOT_GIVEN_hint: A rule only applies to certain ICMP types; the type is not given.
unknown.VIP_AS_INTERFACE_ADDRESS_hint: A virtual IP was used as the interface address. Whether the rule covers it is unclear.
unknown.QUICK_UNKNOWN_hint: For one rule it is unclear whether it decides immediately.
unknown.RECEIVED_ON_hint: A rule only applies to packets received on a certain interface; that is not known on the egress side.
unknown.ACTION_UNKNOWN_hint: The action of a rule could not be determined.
unknown.IFACE_UNRESOLVED_hint: An interface group could not be mapped to its members.
unknown.GROUPS_UNAVAILABLE_hint: Interface groups could not be read.

assumptions.FIRST_PACKET_hint: The first packet of a new connection is evaluated. Replies and established connections follow state, not rules.
assumptions.SRC_PORT_EPHEMERAL_hint: Without a source port, any port from the ephemeral range is assumed.

guiAccess.title: Firewall interface through OPNexus
guiAccess.intro: Opens the web interface of a managed firewall in its own browser tab through OPNexus, even when the firewall is only reachable over the management tunnel. Admins only; you still sign in on the firewall itself. The ticket works once for 30 seconds, every session has time limits and is logged in the audit. Details: manual (German), chapter “Firewall-Oberfläche über OPNexus”.
guiAccess.defaultOff: Off by default. It is set up on the server (Compose profile “gui”, OPNEXUS_GUI_SITES, GUI_GATEWAY_TOKEN) – see the manual (German), chapter “Firewall-Oberfläche über OPNexus”.

reason.gateway_token: Access token for the GUI gateway service (GUI_GATEWAY_TOKEN, at least 32 characters)
reason.gui_sites: Ports for the firewall interfaces (OPNEXUS_GUI_SITES) and the Compose profile “gui”

guiAccess.enabledTip: Turns the feature on for all admins. Turning it off ends open sessions (within about 20 seconds).
guiAccess.idleTip: A session ends after this many minutes without activity (1 to 240). Must not exceed the total duration.
guiAccess.absoluteTip: Every session ends after this time at the latest, even when active (5 to 720).

guiAccess.orderError: The inactivity limit must not exceed the total duration.

guiOpen.opened: Opening the interface in a new tab (slot {slot}). If nothing happens, allow pop-ups for this site.

cleanup.loadFailed: The cleanup list could not be loaded.

form.title: Cleanup: firewall and threshold
form.thresholdHint: How long a rule may go without a hit (or stay disabled and unchanged) before it shows up as a candidate. OPNexus can only look back as far as it has been watching the rule.
form.refreshHint: Re-reads rules, interfaces and aliases from the firewall instead of using the cache (60 s).

cleanup.watching: OPNexus has been counting this firewall's hits since {when}. {collecting} rule(s) are still being watched and cannot count as unused yet.
cleanup.notWatching: OPNexus has not collected rule counters from this firewall yet. Unused rules only show up after the observation period.

notes.ORDER_GUESSED_hint: This OPNsense version delivers no sort order; the order was derived from group and sequence number. Findings about shadowed and duplicate rules are at most probable.
notes.ORDER_MISMATCH_hint: The loaded pf order does not match the rules' sort order. Read findings about shadowed rules with care.
notes.PF_RULESET_UNAVAILABLE_hint: The rule set pf has loaded could not be read, so it is not certain whether a rule is active at all. Nothing is "sure".
notes.GROUPS_UNAVAILABLE_hint: The interface groups could not be read; rules on groups cannot be compared.
notes.ALIASES_UNAVAILABLE_hint: The aliases could not be read; rules using aliases cannot be compared.
notes.NAT_UNAVAILABLE_hint: The port forwards could not be read (irrelevant for cleanup).
notes.CLUSTER_PEER_USAGE_UNKNOWN_hint: For at least one rule a cluster node has no counter data. "Unused" is then "probable" at best.
notes.UNUSED_BLOCK_RULE_hint: A block rule without hits can still protect (rare attacks). So “unused” counts as probable at most here.
notes.UNUSED_WINDOW_SHORT_hint: Under 30 days of observation, monthly and quarterly jobs are missing. “Unused” counts as probable at most.
notes.EXTERNAL_CHANGE_hint: The rule or the rule that shadows it was changed outside OPNexus during the observation period. The finding counts as probable at most.
notes.ENABLE_MAY_BLOCK_MANAGEMENT_hint: A block rule that is not proven to leave the management access alone. Switching it on needs an explicit acknowledgement.

empty.title: No candidates
empty.description: No rule on this firewall is shadowed, duplicate, unused for {days} days or disabled for that long.

category.unused_hint: OPNexus has not observed a single hit of this rule within the threshold (pf counters, read every 15 minutes).
category.shadowed_hint: An earlier rule with "quick" already matches everything this rule matches. This rule never decides.
category.duplicate_hint: An earlier rule matches exactly the same traffic and has the same action.
category.disabled_long_hint: The rule is disabled and OPNexus has seen it unchanged like that for the whole threshold.

tip.sure: Proven: the data is complete and current, none of it rests on an assumption.
tip.probable: Rests on an assumption (e.g. alias content, guessed order, the rule's schedule or a missing pf rule set). Check before removing.
tip.unknown: There is a hint but no proof (e.g. the rule is not loaded in pf or the counters are stale). Do not rely on it.

cleanup.noHitSince: OPNexus has been watching this rule since {when} and has seen no hit.

notRemovable.automatic_hint: OPNsense generates this rule itself and it cannot be removed on its own.
notRemovable.legacy_hint: The rule is still in the old format. Migrate it to the new rule format in OPNsense first.
notRemovable.managed_hint: OPNexus deployed this rule. It is removed through the normal flow of the rules page, otherwise OPNexus would create it again.
notRemovable.confidence_hint: There is a hint but no proof. Such rules are never offered for removal.
notRemovable.nothing_hint: There is no finding for this rule that would justify disabling it.
notRemovable.deleteWait_hint: Only rules that have been disabled long enough, unchanged, and count as sure are deleted. Not reached yet.
notRemovable.unreadable_hint: The rule has no UUID in the new rule format and cannot be changed individually.

select.locked: Locked until management sources are set.
select.busy: Another cleanup is still open: confirm or revert it first.
select.otherKind: One cleanup cannot mix disabling and deleting. Clear the other selection first.
select.needsAckHint: The finding rests on an assumption. Before the preview you confirm for this rule explicitly that it is not needed.

settings.title: Rule cleanup
settings.intro: Limits and protection for disabling, deleting and restoring rules under Analysis, Cleanup.
settings.sourcesHint: Addresses or networks the firewalls are managed from (OPNexus itself, your workstation, a jump host). A rule that could match access from there to the firewall is never disabled. Without an entry the cleanup is locked. IP addresses or networks (CIDR) only, no names.
settings.sourcesInvalid: “{value}” is not an IP address or network (e.g. 203.0.113.10 or 198.51.100.0/24). Host names are not allowed.
settings.sourcesEverything: “{value}” covers the whole address space and would protect every rule.
settings.maxRulesHint: The most rules a single cleanup may change (1 to 25).
settings.minDaysHint: How long a rule that was confirmed as disabled has to stay unchanged before it may be deleted (1 to 365).
settings.portsHint: TCP ports the firewalls are additionally managed on (e.g. SSH or the web GUI on another port). The API port, 443, 80 and 22 are always protected.

mgmt.title: Cleanup locked: management sources missing
mgmt.text: Enter the addresses your firewalls are managed from. After that the cleanup never switches off a rule that could match this access.
mgmt.hint: For every selected rule OPNexus checks whether it can match a packet from a management source to the firewall's management address and port. If it matches, or this cannot be ruled out, the rule is left alone. IP addresses or networks (CIDR) only.
mgmt.askAdmin: An administrator has to enter the management sources in the settings.

intro.disable: The rules on {host} are only disabled, not deleted, and the change is applied.
intro.enable: The rules on {host} are switched on again and the change is applied.
intro.delete: The already disabled rules on {host} are deleted. Their content is backed up first.

introHint.disable: The list was just recomputed from the firewall. When rolling out, OPNexus checks everything again and writes nothing if something changed.
introHint.enable: Switching a rule on can change or block connections. That is why there is a confirmation window again. The list was just recomputed from the firewall.
introHint.delete: A disabled rule is not loaded in the firewall, so deleting it changes nothing there and needs no confirmation window. Under “Cleanup history” the rule can be restored (disabled, at its old position where possible).

preview.loading: Computing the preview from the firewall …
preview.failed: The preview could not be computed.
preview.expired: The preview has expired. Please recompute it.
preview.clusterOrder: Cluster: backup first, then master. Reverting runs in reverse order.
preview.basisDisabled: Disabled by hand and unchanged for a long time.
preview.externalHint: The rule was changed outside OPNexus since it has been observed.
preview.autoRevert: Afterwards you have {window} to check that everything works and the firewall is reachable. If you do not confirm in that time, OPNexus reverts the change automatically.
preview.confirmNameHint: Type the firewall's name exactly. This prevents changing the wrong firewall by accident.
preview.confirmNameAria: Type the firewall name to confirm: {host}
preview.deployDisabledName: The name has to match the firewall's name exactly.
preview.deployNotAdmin: Only administrators may roll out. A preview belongs to whoever created it: an administrator has to open a new preview themselves.

ack.title: These findings rest on an assumption. Acknowledge each rule on its own.
ack.text: Not proven: schedule, alias content or observation period are estimated. I have checked that the rule “{rule}” is not needed.
ack.enableTitle: Switching these block rules on may hit the management access. Acknowledge each rule.
ack.enableText: I checked that switching on “{rule}” does not block OPNexus or the admins from reaching the firewall.

protect.false_hint: No management source ({sources}) can use this rule to reach the firewall's management (checked: {queries} combinations of source, destination, port and interface).
protect.true_hint: The rule can match access from a management source ({sources}) to the firewall. The confirmation window is the safeguard here.
protect.unknown_hint: It could not be ruled out that the rule affects access from a management source ({sources}). The confirmation window is the safeguard here.

toast.deployedConfirm: Applied. Check the firewall now and confirm, otherwise it is reverted.
toast.deployedCheck: Not complete: details in the box above.

revert.reverted: Reverted. The rules are as they were.
revert.revert_failed: Reverting failed. Check the firewall's state.

retry.reverted: Reverted. The rules are as they were.
retry.failed: State checked again, not everything is complete.

ended.failed: The cleanup has ended, but not everything worked.

state.running: OPNexus is writing the change to the firewall. The automatic revert is already armed.
state.awaiting_confirm: The change is applied on the firewall. Check that everything works and the firewall is reachable, then confirm.
state.partial: Not all rules could be changed. Confirming is locked: revert now or wait for the automatic revert.
state.apply_failed: The rules are changed, but applying on the firewall failed. Revert now or wait for the automatic revert.
state.revert_failed: Reverting failed. The firewall's state is unclear: check it in OPNsense and try again.
state.failed: The outcome is unclear for at least one rule. “Check again” makes OPNexus read the firewall's state.

op.countdownMinutes: About {n} min left until the automatic revert.
op.confirmNotYet: Confirming is possible once the change is applied.
op.confirmPartial: Confirming is locked because at least one rule failed or is unclear.
op.confirmApplyFailed: Confirming is locked because applying on the firewall failed.
op.revertNeedsAdmin: Only administrators may revert (setting: operators may roll out).
op.autoRevertNote: Confirming means: you can still reach the firewall. If you do not confirm, OPNexus reverts automatically when the time is up. Confirming works from the browser session only, not with an API token.

status.running_hint: OPNexus is writing to the firewall.
status.awaiting_confirm_hint: Applied. Without confirmation OPNexus reverts automatically when the time is up.
status.confirmed_hint: Confirmed by a user. The change stays.
status.partial_hint: Not all rules could be changed. Revert or wait for the automatic revert.
status.apply_failed_hint: The rules are changed, but the firewall did not apply the change.
status.reverting_hint: OPNexus is restoring the old state.
status.reverted_hint: The old state is restored. The rules' observation window starts again.
status.revert_failed_hint: The firewall's state is unclear. Check it and try again.
status.failed_hint: Not everything was carried out. Details at the rules.
status.cancelled_hint: The preview was not rolled out.
status.expired_hint: The preview was no longer valid.

hist.title: Cleanup history
hist.empty: Nothing has been cleaned up on this firewall yet.
hist.restoreHint: Recreates the deleted rule from the backup, disabled and at its old position where possible.
hist.deleteHint: Opens the preview for deleting this disabled rule.
hist.deleteWait: Deleting is possible from {when} (waiting time after the confirmation, configurable).
hist.enableHint: Opens the preview for switching the rule on, with a confirmation window.

restore.title: Restore rule
restore.intro: The deleted rule is recreated from the backup, disabled and at its old position where possible.
restore.introHint: The rule gets a new UUID. In a cluster it is restored on every node. Switching it on is a separate step (“Enable again”) with a confirmation window. If aliases or categories of the rule are gone meanwhile, the firewall refuses and its message appears in the result.
restore.next: To switch it on: choose “Enable again” under “Cleanup history”.

ruleHistory.since: OPNexus has been watching this firewall since {when}.

empty.since: This rule has not changed since {when}.

origin.opnexus_hint: The change matches a deployment or rollback by OPNexus (an audit entry in that period).

configCode.title: Configuration as code
configCode.intro: Exports rules, NAT, aliases, groups, hierarchy and site variables as one YAML file – for Git, reviews and restoring onto a new instance. Importing only changes the drafts in OPNexus. Firewalls still only receive something through preview → deploy → confirm. The file contains no firewall credentials, users or keys.
configCode.planFailed: The file could not be checked
configCode.tooLarge: The file is larger than 1 MiB.

export.title: Export
export.text: All central objects as opnexus-config.yaml, sorted and without a timestamp, so Git shows real changes only.
export.tip: On the server: opnexus export --out /srv/opnexus-config. With cron or a timer plus git commit this becomes a change log. apply --dry-run checks a file in CI.

import.title: Check and apply a file
import.text: A plan comes first: what would be new, change or be removed. Only then can the file be taken over into the drafts.
import.prune: Remove objects not in the file (prune)
import.pruneTip: Reconciles every kind that appears in the file completely: objects missing from the file are removed from OPNexus. Deployed or still-referenced objects are never removed, they block the plan.

configCode.noDifferencesText: The file matches the current state in OPNexus.
configCode.blockedHint: The plan contains blocked objects and cannot be applied as it is. Fix the cause, or take the objects out of the file and plan again.
configCode.deployedOn: Deployed on {n} firewall(s): redeploy through the preview afterwards.
configCode.implicit: Follows from order or membership, not in the file.

reason.busy_deployment: Open deployment: confirm or roll it back first
reason.prune_deployed: Is deployed: remove it in the interface first

warn.redeploy_needed: {count} changed objects are deployed: redeploy them through the preview after applying.
warn.targets_without_link: {count} new objects have targets but are not linked to objects on the firewalls: deploying may create duplicates. Link them first or restore from a full backup.
warn.unknown_alias_reference: "{value}" looks like an alias, but no such alias exists.
warn.variable_removed_in_use: Variable {name} of {host} is removed while an object still uses it (deploying to that host will then fail).

confirm.title: Apply the plan?
confirm.nothingOnFirewalls: Nothing is written to firewalls. The changes appear as drafts and are deployed as usual through preview → deploy → confirm.
confirm.prune: {n} objects will be removed from OPNexus.

configCode.appliedNext: Nothing was written to firewalls. Now deploy the drafts object by object through preview → deploy → confirm.
